facts.statement: The genus Omnivoropteryx was described by Czerkas and Ji in 2002.
Omnivoropteryx lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
Stephen Czerkas and Qiang Ji were the authors who described the genus Omnivoropteryx.
Fossils of Omnivoropteryx were found in the Upper Jiufotang Formation of China from the early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: early Cretaceous Upper Jiufotang Formation of China

facts.statement: It is debated whether Omnivoropteryx is a junior synonym of Sapeornis and should be abandoned.
facts.quote: This may make Omnivoropteryx a junior synonym of Sapeornis, and the name may be abandoned.

facts.statement: Czerkas and Ji established the family Omnivoropterygidae and the order Omnivoropterygiformes to include the genus Omnivoropteryx.
facts.quote: Czerkas and Ji created the family Omnivoropterygidae to contain the genus Omnivoropteryx, as well as the order Omnivoropterygiformes

facts.statement: Some scientists argue that the family Omnivoropterygidae is invalid because it contains only a single genus.
facts.quote: some scientists do not recognize taxa that contain only one genus

facts.statement: Omnivoropteryx had short legs adapted for perching and long wings.
facts.quote: the legs were short and well suited for perching on branches, while the wings were long

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Omnivoropteryx was an opportunistic omnivore capable of utilizing a wide range of food sources.
facts.quote: Thus, the species may have been an opportunistic omnivore (as the name suggests), utilizing a wide range of food sources

facts.statement: Omnivoropteryx lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The skull of Omnivoropteryx resembled early oviraptorosaurs, featuring a beak designed for crushing and tearing with teeth at the tip of the upper jaw.
rejected.quote: Its skull, on the other hand, was similar to some early oviraptorosaurs, having the structure of a beak designed for crushing and tearing with some teeth at the tip of the upper jaw
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'a beak designed for crushing and tearing with'
